headline: UN report: US committed war crimes in Iran; Washington rejects findings
summary: The US State Department and White House have dismissed a UN investigation into missile strikes that killed over 170 civilians, including 120 school children.
details: A UN independent international fact-finding mission has found evidence that the United States committed war crimes during the conflict in Iran.
The report highlights a Tomahawk missile strike on a primary school in Minab, which killed more than 150 people, including at least 120 students according to Iranian officials.
Another attack on a residential area and a sports facility killed 22 civilians, with the UN noting the targets were easily identifiable as non-military.
The US State Department has rejected the findings, stating that it does not find the results of the report credible.
Washington claims the UN Human Rights Council spreads anti-US sentiment and antisemitism, and that it protects oppressive regimes.
The White House has also dismissed the report, with spokesperson Anna Kelly stating that only the Iranian leadership has committed war crimes in this conflict.
President Donald Trump had previously withdrawn the US from the UN Human Rights Council in February 2025 via executive order, citing interests contrary to US interests.
caption:
Over 170 civilians, including 120 school children, killed in US strikes. The UN says they are war crimes; the US says the report is not credible.

A UN independent international fact-finding mission has found evidence that the United States committed war crimes during the conflict in Iran.

The report highlights a Tomahawk missile strike on a primary school in Minab, which killed more than 150 people, including at least 120 students according to Iranian officials.

Another attack on a residential area and a sports facility killed 22 civilians, with the UN noting the targets were easily identifiable as non-military.

The US State Department has rejected the findings, stating that it does not find the results of the report credible.

Washington claims the UN Human Rights Council spreads anti-US sentiment and antisemitism, and that it protects oppressive regimes.

The White House has also dismissed the report, with spokesperson Anna Kelly stating that only the Iranian leadership has committed war crimes in this conflict.

President Donald Trump had previously withdrawn the US from the UN Human Rights Council in February 2025 via executive order, citing interests contrary to US interests.

headline: Defying Global Powers: Houthi rebels grow stronger despite a decade of attacks
summary: Saudi Arabia, UAE, US, UK, and Israel have launched extensive strikes against the group in Yemen, yet the Houthis continue to expand their military capabilities.
details: Over the last decade, the Houthi rebels in Yemen have faced massive military campaigns from a coalition of global powers including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Israel.
Despite these extensive attacks and sustained pressure, the group has not been weakened; instead, they have emerged as a more powerful military force.
The group's ability to survive and grow in the face of such overwhelming opposition highlights a significant shift in regional stability and military dynamics.
Observers are now analyzing how the Houthis managed to build their capabilities and sustain their operations despite being targeted by some of the world's most advanced militaries.
